must_catch.item: The outcome carries the online-only scope note
The decision-maker contradiction is surfaced (Maya chose, Greg decided)
Customer language is marked Not covered

data.notes: The report's biggest strength is that it never overstates the win. The header scope note is exactly right: online billing only, front desk still on Global, phase two undated. It also surfaces the Maya-chose/Greg-decided contradiction and correctly hangs the win on value proof shown on the customer's own file. Its biggest miss is that the language section is flagged covered:true even though its own text admits the question was deferred to Slack, so it was never formally marked Not covered. Smaller misses: the trigger section leaves out Maya's 'members who never meant to leave' quote and the link to the controller. The competitor messaging retreats from in-store when the key treats the front desk as the phase-two battleground. The close and messaging never frame the front desk as a live open deal or call for proof of a reader working live in their own studio software.
